entry.title: A shared room can serve different ages
entry.summary: Davies makes room for children to share a home while protecting materials and personal space. A younger child’s access does not have to match an older child’s.
entry.cue: One child reaches for another’s work, or a shared room needs clearer places.
detail: Her storage examples keep older children’s small parts genuinely out of younger children’s reach, or in containers the younger child cannot open. If an activity can be simplified for the younger child, that is a separate way to join.
She also describes places for personal belongings and for being alone, with clear agreements about using a shared space. This is different from sending an upset toddler away.
For small homes, fewer displayed items and useful storage can create room. The purpose is a home that works for its people.
